traceability.evidence:
Story file docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md exists and is referenced directly in implementation and tests.
Core plugin structure (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-NPM-PACKAGE): - src/index.ts is the TypeScript entry point with JSDoc: """ /** * ESLint Traceability Plugin * @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md * @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Provide foundational plugin export and registration * @req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING - Gracefully handles plugin loading errors and missing dependencies */ """ - src/index.ts defines a rule registry and exports in standard ESLint plugin shape: - RULE_NAMES array listing rule modules. - Dynamic loader using require(`./rules/${name}`) and building a rules: Record map. - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() providing plugin + rules mapping. - configs = { recommended: [...], strict: [...] }. - Final export: `export { rules, configs, maintenance }; export default { rules, configs, maintenance };`. - All rules exist as TypeScript modules under src/rules/ (require-story-annotation.ts, require-req-annotation.ts, require-branch-annotation.ts, valid-annotation-format.ts, valid-story-reference.ts, valid-req-reference.ts). - tsconfig.json outputs CommonJS to lib/ and generates declarations, and package.json points main and types to lib/src/index.js and lib/src/index.d.ts, with files: ["lib", ...] and proper peerDependencies and engines, satisfying REQ-NPM-PACKAGE. - Built JS artifacts exist (lib/src/index.js and lib/src/rules/require-story-annotation.js), confirming the TypeScript plugin compiles into a Node-loadable npm package.
ESLint v9 flat config integration (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM): - eslint.config.js uses ESLint v9 flat config style (module.exports = [ js.configs.recommended, { files: [...], languageOptions: {...} }, ... ]). - It conditionally requires the plugin from ./src/index.js or ./lib/src/index.js and, if both are missing in CI, throws a clear error; otherwise logs a warning and continues without the plugin. This demonstrates explicit plugin loading behavior and environment-aware error handling. - For TypeScript and JavaScript file globs, it includes the traceability plugin via `plugins: { ...(plugin.rules ? { traceability: plugin } : {}) }` and configures base rules, confirming flat-config integration. - src/index.ts defines configs.recommended and configs.strict as arrays of flat config objects, providing a configuration system for users (REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM).
Error handling (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) and tests: - src/index.ts wraps each dynamic rule require in try/catch, logging a detailed console.error and installing a placeholder RuleModule that reports an ESLint error when a rule fails to load. This is directly aligned with “gracefully handles plugin loading errors”. - eslint.config.js handles missing plugin builds differently for CI vs local dev (error vs warning), covering plugin loading failures and missing dependencies. - tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts (header references this story and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) mocks a rule module to throw, then requires ../src/index and asserts: - console.error called with text containing 'Failed to load rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error'. - plugin.rules["require-branch-annotation"] is defined and its meta.docs.description includes the failure text. - The placeholder rule's create() visitor reports an error message containing 'Error loading rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error'. - tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts (also tagged with this story and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) spawns ESLint CLI with eslint.config.js and asserts non-zero exit status and the expected missing-@story error message on stdout when running with traceability rules enabled.
Core functionality & integration (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-TEST-SETUP): - tests/plugin-setup.test.ts (annotated with this story and REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE) imports plugin, { rules, configs } from ../src/index and asserts that rules/configs are defined objects and plugin.rules === rules, plugin.configs === configs. This verifies that the plugin exports are wired correctly. - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts (annotated with this story and REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE) uses child_process.spawnSync to run ESLint’s CLI with the project’s eslint.config.js and various traceability rules. It checks exit codes for multiple scenarios (missing/present @story, missing @req, invalid/path-traversal references), proving that: - The plugin loads successfully via ESLint CLI using the flat config. - Rules are registered and enforce behavior as expected. - jest.config.js configures ts-jest, testMatch for tests/**/*.test.ts, coverage thresholds, and other Jest settings, and tsconfig.json includes tests and Jest types, satisfying REQ-TEST-SETUP as a testing infrastructure for the plugin and its rules.
Documentation, user experience, and quality standards: - README.md provides: - Installation instructions using npm and Yarn. - ESLint v9 flat config examples using this plugin, including a quick start where `traceability.configs.recommended` is consumed. - Usage examples showing how to annotate functions with @story and run ESLint. - Commands for running tests and quality checks (npm test, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm run duplication). - Links to user-docs (eslint-9-setup-guide, api-reference, examples, migration-guide) and development documentation. - docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md outlines plugin structure, meta, rule design, testing guidelines, TS and package.json settings, and recommended development practices, aligning with ESLint plugin best practices and conventions.
Test execution evidence: - Running `npm test -- --verbose` executes `jest --ci --bail --verbose` with no reported failures or errors in the captured output, indicating the suite (including plugin-setup and error-handling tests) is passing under the configured runner. - Running `npm test -- --runInBand tests/plugin-setup.test.ts tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts --verbose` shows Jest invoked with those files and no subsequent error output, consistent with those story-specific tests passing.
Collectively, this confirms: the ESLint plugin loads and exports rules/configs, integrates with ESLint v9 flat config, supports configuration presets, is packaged as a proper npm module, has a TypeScript-based implementation, includes targeted tests (unit + integration) specifically tied to this story, implements robust error handling for plugin and rule loading, and provides user and developer documentation for setup and development.
